reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the output contract, resource assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, the OperationDefinition resource-review context, the full local StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate, and the in-scope behavior material. The direct behavior finding is the SearchParameter canonical consolidation whose `affectedResources` include `OperationDefinition`; shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings were considered as context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 OperationDefinition is normative/FMM 5, so even targeted required-binding and error-constraint breaks need a clear compatibility rationale. That does not forbid all R6 tightening, but it raises the value of low-cost aliases, deprecated codes, and semantic-preservation designs for operation conformance metadata.

overall.oneLineConclusion: OperationDefinition keeps its identity and general shape, but R6 introduces targeted hard terminology and validation breaks, so catalog migration is partly unavoidable while low-cost compatibility preservation remains important.

reasoning.thesisMd: OperationDefinition is not removed, renamed, split, or wholesale remodeled. The dominant R4-to-R6 migration is a targeted conformance-metadata cleanup: required-bound type/resource code domains change, named-query shapes become error-constrained, parameter cardinality/searchType rules tighten, and several R6-only operation-signature semantics need conversion policy. Because the artifact is normative/FMM 5 and drives executable operation contracts, this is more than routine codegen churn even though it is not a resource replacement.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: Most existing paths remain recognizable and no local R4 element was removed. However, serious OperationDefinition publishers cannot simply switch validators: they must inventory `parameter.type` and `resource` codes, decide mappings for removed or retired R4 resources/types, normalize named-query definitions to the R6 shape, repair malformed cardinalities and output `searchType`, and decide how to carry R6-only `synchronicity`, `parameter.scope`, `allowedType`, canonical metadata, and `descriptive` binding strength when downgrading or round-tripping. This is a moderate targeted remodel rather than a major model replacement.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A migration program is already needed for non-trivial catalogs, but that does not make additional break prevention low value. OperationDefinition is infrastructure used by validators, generated SDKs, CapabilityStatements, operation routing, documentation, and conformance tests. Preserving old resource-scope codes, avoiding silent semantic drift in `jurisdiction`, and providing SearchParameter canonical aliases would materially reduce migration risk without undermining the main R6 operation-model goals.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest low-cost preservation candidates are including all R4 resource codes in the R6 version-independent resource-type value set with retired/legacy lifecycle metadata, keeping `jurisdiction` as intended-use jurisdiction while adding or formalizing a separate maintaining-authority signal, and publishing deprecated canonical SearchParameter aliases for per-resource OperationDefinition search parameters. By contrast, keeping obsolete `parameter.type` codes base-valid, weakening named-query constraints to warnings, or allowing nonsensical cardinalities would materially reduce R6 computability and are better treated as migration chores unless stronger standards rationale emerges.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The one direct behavior finding does not remove OperationDefinition queries, but it changes canonical SearchParameter identity for metadata-resource searches. That matters for CapabilityStatement.searchParam.definition, registries, generated clients, and conformance tests that key on canonical URLs. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` operation and special-search findings remain background context only for this assigned resource, not independent drivers of the OperationDefinition resource conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's broad conclusion: `Partial`, `moderate-targeted-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. The independent basis is not the raw count of five hard breaks alone; it is the concentration of those breaks in executable operation metadata plus the strong normative/FMM 5 stability pressure and the presence of a few plausible low-cost compatibility mechanisms.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the local StructureDefinition and behavior-report facts. Remaining uncertainty is mainly prevalence and intent: no production OperationDefinition corpus, official HL7 migration rationale, authoritative terminology-server expansions, or final R6 package was used.

findingConsiderations.title: parameter.type required binding changed from R4 all-types to R6 fhir-types
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real old-valid/new-invalid required-binding break for operation parameters that name R4-only or retired type/resource codes, and it also creates downgrade loss for R6-only types. It drives migration planning, but accepting non-native obsolete type names in base R6 would weaken the computability of current-version operation signatures, so it is less clearly a low-cost standards-preservation candidate than the `resource` binding.

findingConsiderations.title: resource required binding omits several R4 resource codes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `OperationDefinition.resource` controls where an operation is exposed, and R6's version-independent value set still omits multiple R4 resource codes. Because a retired/legacy-code inclusion strategy appears compatible with the version-independent goal, this is both a migration driver and a standards-review-worthy low-cost preservation opportunity.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds hard shape constraints for named queries
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 query OperationDefinitions with instance-level invocation, missing input `searchType`, or non-standard output shape can become invalid. This meaningfully contributes to a resource-level migration program, but the R6 goal of making named queries uniformly computable is strong; warning-only or profile-only alternatives would not give base R6 clients the same guarantee.

findingConsiderations.title: Parameter cardinality values are now non-negative, numeric, and internally consistent
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can reject R4-valid lexical forms such as negative `min`, non-numeric `max`, or `min > max`, but those forms describe malformed operation contracts. It should be included in migration validation, not treated as a strong reason to preserve the old permissive base rules.

findingConsiderations.title: searchType is now input-only and gains R6 code resource
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The old-valid/new-invalid part is limited to output parameters carrying `searchType`; the R6-only `resource` code is a downgrade issue. This is real validator and generator work, but the input-only rule is a defensible cleanup of ambiguous output metadata.

findingConsiderations.title: jurisdiction changes from intended use to maintaining authority
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not a validation break, but it is a same-path semantic change on a normative resource: R4 intended-use jurisdiction can be silently reinterpreted as maintaining-authority jurisdiction in R6. A separate maintaining-authority element or explicit `useContext` convention would preserve old meaning with modest added metadata surface.

findingConsiderations.title: affectsState GET guidance now considers required primitive parameters
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This changes runtime conformance expectations for safe operations with required primitive parameters and optional complex parameters. It deserves implementer guidance and tests, but it appears to clarify a useful GET-support rule rather than create a broad instance migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds synchronicity invocation semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The optional addition is not a forward validation break, but it captures operationally important sync/async behavior that R4 cannot natively round-trip. Migration tooling should preserve it through extensions or sidecar metadata when downgrading, while core R6 support is proportionate.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds parameter.scope for system/type/instance applicability
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Like `synchronicity`, this optional field does not invalidate R4 instances but adds useful computable invocation-level semantics. It is a conversion and generated-client concern, not a reason to lower the value of preserving avoidable hard R4-to-R6 breaks elsewhere.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 promotes operationdefinition-allowed-type extension to parameter.allowedType
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a documented promotion of an R4 extension to an optional core element. Converters need explicit extension-to-core and core-to-extension mapping, but the change is not an R4-to-R6 base invalidation and should not drive the resource-level break posture.

findingConsiderations.title: OperationDefinition.code is now a recommended URL label, not necessarily the invocation name
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The R6 wording can surprise clients that treated `code` as the only invocation token, but the CapabilityStatement override/name-clash model already existed. This is mainly discovery guidance: clients should resolve concrete operation names from CapabilityStatement when available.

findingConsiderations.title: parameter.documentation changes from string to markdown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The wire value remains string-shaped and ordinary R4 text remains valid markdown content. Generated primitive wrappers and rendering/sanitization paths may change, but this is low-risk tooling churn rather than a material resource-level migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: OperationDefinition is one of the affected metadata resources. Runtime query codes usually remain available, but canonical SearchParameter URLs are conformance identities; deprecated per-resource aliases or equivalence guidance would be a low-cost way to reduce registry, CapabilityStatement, and generated-client churn.

findingConsiderations.title: Base CapabilityStatement removed several R4 system-level operation advertisements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource-level operation-advertisement finding is relevant background for operation discovery tooling, but its `affectedResources` do not include OperationDefinition and the review rules keep shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior as context only for this assigned resource.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Generic `$validate` behavior may affect validators used on OperationDefinition instances, but it is a Resource-level operation behavior rather than an OperationDefinition-specific structure or direct behavior finding. It should be handled in the shared Resource/operation review stream.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Ask standards reviewers to revisit the two strongest low-cost compatibility opportunities: include all R4 resource-scope codes in the R6 version-independent resource-type value set with retired/legacy metadata, and avoid same-path semantic drift for `jurisdiction` by preserving intended-use semantics or adding a distinct maintaining-authority signal.

Publish OperationDefinition R4-to-R6 migration guidance and tests covering `parameter.type` and `resource` code mapping, named-query constraints, parameter cardinality repairs, output `searchType` cleanup, `affectsState` GET expectations, and downgrade handling for `synchronicity`, `parameter.scope`, `allowedType`, and canonical metadata.

Provide conformance-metadata transition guidance for OperationDefinition search: deprecated/equivalent canonical SearchParameter aliases, and client matching by base/code/type/expression rather than canonical URL alone.

Confirm the `all-types`, `fhir-types`, `resource-types`, and `version-independent-all-resource-types` comparisons with authoritative terminology expansions and publish ConceptMaps for removed, renamed, retired, and R6-only codes.

caveats: The R6 input is 6.0.0-ballot4 and may change before final publication.
Terminology conclusions rely on local package ValueSet/CodeSystem data rather than authoritative terminology-server expansions.
No real-world corpus of R4 OperationDefinition instances was validated, so prevalence is qualitative.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context, per the resource-review rules.
